summary: ```markdown # Modular Library Update | Clo Feature Deep Dive Hi all you Clovers! My name is Phoebe, and I'm going to show you the update that we did to Modular, specifically how we optimized it so that there's now only one Modular library. I'll explain what that means for all the old Modular blocks and how it'll all work, along with some updates we've made to our settings for Modular. I know you're as excited as I am, so let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Overview of the Modular Library Update So, as many of you might know, we've streamlined our Modular library to just one location. This means you don't have to figure out which library to go into; it's all consolidated into one now. You can access the Modular library and find categories for kids, men, and women. We already have some blocks ready for you, and you can also create and bring in your own. There’s a comprehensive tutorial on Modular that covers everything in-depth. ## Using the Optimized Modular Library ### Importing Old Modular Library Files I'm bringing in a file that actually uses the old Modular library files, and I'm going to drop this in. What happens, you may ask? A pop-up window appears, indicating that Clo acknowledges this file is from an older Modular library. It confirms that it will still be modular and will load automatically. However, don't be fooled; this doesn’t mean the file will magically appear in your Modular library. You still need to specify where you want it saved. For instance, if you brought in a pair of pants, we wouldn’t want to automatically categorize it under shirts, right? You have to decide where to place it in your Modular library. ### Setting Default Folders Now, let’s talk about settings. If I go into settings, then user settings, and navigate to "Other," I can access the Modular library settings. Here, I can choose where I want my default folder to be. For example, I can set it to save in a folder on my desktop called "Testing Modular." This feature is beneficial for large companies or individuals who want to keep everything organized in one place. ## Saving and Organizing Modular Files I have this shirt that’s modular, but I still need to specify how I want to save it. I can go to "File," select "Save As," and then choose a category such as men's, women's, or kids. I can also add my own categories. As I do this, it automatically directs me to my "Testing Modular" folder, as that’s the default I set earlier. ### Adding New Items Next, I can create a new folder, select the category, and add it. For example, I can add blocks such as the front body, back body, sleeves, collar, and cuffs. After selecting each part, I can even include an image if I want. Once I've set everything up, I can check my taglines and confirm that everything looks wonderful. ## Finalizing and Accessing Your Modular Library Now, I can go back to my Modular library in my practice area. Everything is organized as intended, and I can verify it on my desktop under the "Testing Modular" folder. All items will save correctly, and the workflow is straightforward. You just need to choose where you want to save everything, and the old files will still load in as needed. If you have any questions about this update, feel free to leave them in the comment section. Thank you for watching, and don't forget to continue using our YouTube channel—it's filled with so many great videos. Thanks again! ```
